ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 August 2019 on the RBE register; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector, as amended

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport for each UBO, legal representative and shareholder acting as an individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing passport authority or a licensed notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the country is party to the Hague Convention of 1961; otherwise Consular Legalization at the relevant Luxembourg diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Recent proof of residential address for each individual UBO and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public utility provider or a regulated bank in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized translation into French, German or Luxembourgish with Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing for each corporate shareholder or parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry or corporate registrar in the shareholder's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the board resolution or power of attorney appointing the representative who will sign the notarial deed of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the appointing corporate entity or a notary in the company's country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence covering the identification, verification and continuous screening of all UBOs against the Luxembourg national sanctions list, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, and applicable domestic PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates in accordance with the amended Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02. Adverse media screening and ongoing transaction filtering are applied for the entire duration of the client relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be formed using Latin alphabet characters. The registered name may use French, German, Luxembourgish or an internationally recognized language, but must end with the legal form suffix 's.à r.l.' or 'SARL'. Names must not be false, misleading, contrary to public order or public morality. Non-Latin scripts require an official transliteration into Latin characters. The articles of association must be prepared in French, German or Luxembourgish, and all documents in foreign languages must be translated by a sworn translator into one of those languages.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Finance / Financial requiring prior approval by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance / Reinsurance requiring prior approval by the Commissariat aux Assurances
Fonds / Fund / Investment Fund implying regulated investment vehicles requiring CSSF or Ministry of Finance clearance
Luxembourg / État / Municipal / Commune / Chamber of Commerce implying state patronage or public institutional affiliation
Any name identical or confusingly similar to a name already registered in the RCS
Any name contrary to public order or public morals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS registrar rejects the proposed name, the applicant or its notary may submit a reasoned request for administrative reconsideration to the RCS within 15 days of the rejection notification. If the reconsideration is unsuccessful, an administrative appeal may be filed before the Minister of Justice within one month. Judicial recourse is available before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, civil chamber, within 40 days from notification of the final administrative decision. The initial 30-day name reservation window is not extended ex officio; a fresh name clearance application must be filed after expiry or if the proposed name is rejected.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A fully virtual office is not acceptable for an RCS-registered SARL. Commercial domiciliation with a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation company is permissible provided that the SARL has a physical registered address in Luxembourg where company books, records and statutory documentation can be maintained and where directors, managers and authorized representatives are accessible. A pure mail-forwarding virtual office without any Luxembourg substance is not sufficient for incorporation, RCS registration, tax residence or AML compliance purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_Probability_Below_10_Percent_First_Year. Unannounced on-site inspections remain possible through the tax administration, the RCS, social security authorities and AML supervisory bodies, particularly if nominee director arrangements, domiciliation-only substance or exposure to international sanctions is detected. For the target low-risk, non-licensed vertical ERP/CRM cloud business, the standard baseline risk is low, but the probability rises if the company is selected for an administrative tax audit or if a PEP or adverse media flag appears.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended; SARL provisions Articles 710-1 through 710-25; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers and annual accounts; Grand-Ducal regulations on RCS e-filing and RESA publication.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of incorporation (acte constitutif / statuts), executed in notarized or private-deed form as permitted, together with the electronic RCS registration application filed through LBR.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The minimum subscribed and issued share capital is EUR 12,000. At least 25% of the cash capital, i.e. EUR 3,000, must be paid up before RCS registration. Subscription funds must be deposited in a blocked company-in-formation account held by a Luxembourg credit institution, or an equivalent escrow arrangement, and released only after RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the constitutive meeting held on [date], the founder and sole subscribing shareholder, having approved the draft statutes, adopted the following first board resolutions: (1) the company is incorporated as a Luxembourg société à responsabilité limitée governed by the Law of 10 August 1915; the total subscribed share capital of EUR 12,000 is confirmed and held blocked until RCS registration; (2) the registered office is established at [address] in Luxembourg; (3) [Name] is appointed gérant with sole signature; (4) the gérant is instructed to file the RCS application, procure RESA publication, and complete VAT, EORI, social security and beneficial-owner registrations; (5) all officer appointments take effect on RCS registration. Passed unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital account and bank certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or notary's escrow client account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a company-in-formation account in the intended company name at a Luxembourg bank. Deposit the full subscribed minimum capital of EUR 12,000, or at least EUR 3,000 where the statutes validly provide for partial payment, and instruct the bank to block the funds until the company is legally registered. Obtain the banker's certificate (attestation de blocage) naming the forthcoming company as beneficiary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further KYC information, provide enhanced UBO and negative-media declarations; if the certificate wording is insufficient, require the bank to issue a corrected blocked-funds certificate before notarial execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of articles and adoption of first board resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public, or the shareholders acting directly where a private deed is permitted, followed by filing with LBR.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the constitutive meeting. Approve the final statutes, adopt the pro-forma first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office adoption and gérant appointment, and execute the deed in the chosen statutory form. Ensure all shareholders sign, the gérant accepts the mandate, and the notary, where engaged, provides the authenticated copy for RCS submission.
required_dossiers: Identity documents or residence permits of shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or LBR pre-review identifies defects, execute a corrective deed or rectifying rider before the same parties; adjust the filing package and reperform registration without a fresh RCS refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic RCS registration application and filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online e-filing module with LuxTrust-authenticated signature.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed articles, first board resolutions, banker's certificate and manager declarations to the LBR platform. Pay the applicable state fee, sign all electronic forms with the appointed gérant's LuxTrust certificate, and submit the RCS registration form. Monitor the application in the LBR dashboard for issuance of the dossier number and registration approval.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCS issues a query, respond through the authorised signatory or notary within the specified cure period, usually ten business days, by uploading the corrected deed, revised capital certificate or amended corporate purpose; after cure, LBR continues the registration review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RESA publication and RCS extract delivery
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and the Official Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (RESA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS approval, verify that the legal notice is published in RESA, which acts as the official gazette for corporate acts. Obtain the official RCS extract showing the company registration number, registered office, incorporation date, capital, gérant(s) and business purpose, and use it as the authoritative certificate of incorporation for bank, tax and commercial onboarding.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, file a written follow-up with LBR support; if the RESA notice contains an error, request a corrective rectification publication through the electronic RCS module.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-formation tax, EORI, employer and beneficial-owner registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Luxembourg Business Registers for the RBE; ITM and CCSS for employment; Chambre de Commerce for professional affiliation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File VAT registration with AEDT, apply for EORI, register the company as an employer with the social security authorities, file the beneficial-owner declaration in the RBE, and complete any compulsory Chamber of Commerce formalities. Retain the RCS extract and register payment rails such as Stripe Billing and Direct Debit under the company's Luxembourg VAT number and bank account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEDT rejects the VAT filing, correct the Luxembourg business address, legal-form code or intended activity description and refile; for RBE non-compliance, submit a curative declaration together with the RCS extract and pay any applicable administrative fine if already imposed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No dedicated industrial licensing authority applies to non-physical ISIC 6201 vertical ERP/CRM cloud-software activity; municipal building authority and Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) retain competence for office premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating or manufacturing permit is required; the RCS registration certificate serves as proof of legal operation, complemented by a municipal occupancy permit for the registered office.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement, Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Unclassified activity: pure software and CRM cloud services do not trigger a classified-establishment permit under Luxembourg environmental legislation; no EIA report is required unless the premises include large-scale server halls or substantial standby generators.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office-type operations generate no process wastewater, combustion fumes or VOC emissions; compliance is required for WEEE electronic waste, packaging waste, office waste segregation, and, if backup generators are installed, Grand-Ducal emission sound and exhaust limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupancy permit, fire safety certification, structural load inspection, ITM workplace safety clearance, electricity installation conformity, and any municipal civil-defense signposting must be obtained before continuous office operations commence.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax; official portal is MyGuichet.lu and Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign investor must (1) incorporate the SARL before the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and obtain a national business number ('matricule'); (2) file company incorporation documents and evidence of minimum capital; (3) submit a VAT registration application to the AEDT (form 1 DTV/VA); (4) obtain the Luxembourg VAT identification number ('no. TVA') and corporate tax file number. As a resident SARL, no separate foreign TIN is required. Timeframe: 3-5 weeks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime in Luxembourg. A SARL is mandatorily subject to entity-level corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICB) and net wealth tax (ISF). No fiscal-transparency election is available for a SARL; however, hybrid-mismatch alignment elections under ATAD 2 may apply to cross-border instruments, and certain partnerships may be treated as transparent for Luxembourg tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Luxembourg Value Added Tax (TVA/Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), harmonised under the EU VAT Directive.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (exclusive of VAT) for the domestic small-business exemption. Mandatory VAT registration is nevertheless required for intra-Community acquisitions, distance sales exceeding EUR 10,000 (OSS), certain cross-border B2C digital services, or when exercising the option to apply normal VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API filing or digital stamping applies to general B2B invoicing in Luxembourg. Structured e-invoicing (Factur-X/UBL via PEPPOL) is mandatory only for B2G contracts. Paper and PDF invoices remain valid for VAT; VAT returns are filed electronically through MyGuichet. The EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) package is expected to introduce future mandatory e-invoicing for intra-EU transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to the export of goods physically dispatched/transported to a non-EU destination. For exported services, including cloud CRM/ERP software B2B services, Luxembourg VAT is displaced by the place-of-supply rule: (i) EU B2B customer - reverse charge; (ii) non-EU B2B customer - no Luxembourg VAT if the customer's establishment is outside Luxembourg; (iii) for B2C digital services to non-EU customers, destination rules similarly remove Luxembourg VAT. Eligibility requires documentary proof of recipient identity, establishment and use; absence of abuse; and, for goods, a valid customs export declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/Déclaration en Douane) - required for physical goods; for pure digital services no customs declaration is applicable.
Bill of Lading / CMR / airway bill - transport evidence demonstrating export; for digital services, service contract and delivery evidence are the functional substitute.
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer confirmation showing export proceeds collection, together with invoices and customer VAT number/economic operator status documentation.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may reassess VAT for up to 3 years (5 years on omission, 10 years for fraudulent evasion). Unsubstantiated zero-rating or abusive arrangements trigger clawback of unpaid VAT, default interest (0.8% per month) and fines up to the amount of the evaded tax; criminal penalties for VAT fraud include imprisonment and publication of sanction. Mitigation requires preserving complete customer due diligence and export evidence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem; foreign exchange control and sanctions enforcement are coordinated with the Ministère des Finances and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible without exchange-control restrictions in Luxembourg. Under the EU Treaty and Luxembourg monetary law, both current account and capital account transactions are liberalised. Profit remittances from a Luxembourg SARL may be distributed freely via SEPA or SWIFT rails; the only substantive hurdles are standard anti-money-laundering (AML) identification of the ultimate beneficial owner and possible Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends, which does not require any central bank approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion requirements. Export receipts may be retained in EUR or foreign currency at the exporter's discretion. The only applicable regulatory duty is the statistical balance-of-payments reporting obligation to the BCL, which must be discharged through the reporting bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE) - Spuerkeess

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating for a Luxembourg-resident low-risk software SARL is high for EEA-authorised electronic money institutions (EMIs), which may provide online account opening, SEPA direct debit collection, and cross-border payment services under an EU passport. A wholly offshore digital EMI without a CSSF licence or an EEA passport is legally unacceptable as a primary treasury account. A validly authorised fintech EMI may be used as a non-core payment gateway, provided the principal transaction banking relationship remains with a fully regulated bank in Luxembourg.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not require the physical presence of directors for a low-risk SARL account opening. Remote onboarding is possible through a reliable video-identification process satisfying CSSF AML/KYC expectations. Nevertheless, certain traditional banks retain a policy of at least one in-person meeting for the initial KYC interview. For the described standard cloud software SARL, a remote process accompanied by corporate due-diligence documents and certified copies of beneficial-owner identification is generally accepted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner is a non-resident individual holding more than 25% of the SARL and providing limited proof of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copy of each ultimate beneficial owner; Luxembourg UBO register extract; documented corporate shareholding chain; bank references dated within three months; source-of-wealth file including salary, dividends, sale proceeds, and prior tax returns; an independent legal opinion on the ownership structure; and audited financial statements of the direct shareholder if available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound and outbound wire transfers referencing multiple high-risk jurisdictions for software licences.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master software licensing agreements; itemised and dated invoices matching the payment schedule; export of internal CRM/ERP usage logs or delivery evidence; economic substance documentation showing Luxembourg employees/contractors; transfer pricing documentation prepared in accordance with OECD principles; and a written narrative explanation addressing each payment counterparty's jurisdictional profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A large, one-off MT103 capital injection unexplained by ordinary consultancy revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date shareholders' resolution approving the contribution; notarised capital increase deed or registered capital certificate; bank reference and source-of-funds statements issued by the sending institution; the SARL's updated statutory accounts; and a compliance memo explaining the commercial rationale, targeted liquidity buffer, and future software development expenditure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Positive sanctions list hit or adverse media associated with a legal entity sharing the exact corporate name.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full legal opinion on the actual corporate structure distinguishing the SARL from the sanctioned entity; official Luxembourg commercial register (RCS) abstract with unchanged corporate number; a sanctions-screening rationale giving jurisdiction and issuer of the definitive list; evidence of the true beneficiary's nationality and residence; and, if requested, an independent external audit of transaction flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder equity subscriptions or shareholder loans must be routed through ordinary SWIFT MT103 using the bank's BIC and the SARL's IBAN. The payment instruction should quote the appropriate balance-of-payments statistical purpose code—for instance, subscribed capital contributions or intercompany financing. The receiving Luxembourg bank will notify the BCL under the national statistical reporting framework. Supporting documentation to be held on file includes the shareholder resolution, share subscription agreement, proof of source of funds from the sending bank, and the SARL's official registration details. No prior BCL exchange-control approval is required for EUR transfers originating within the EEA.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For low-value recurring software subscriptions and operating payments, the primary clearing rails are SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Direct Debit. For non-EUR cross-border vendor payments, subcontractor fees, royalties, and intercompany disbursements, the bank executes SWIFT MT103. Commercial letter-of-credit operations, when used for reseller or original-equipment-manufacturer trade, are settled through the MT700/MT400 series under the applicable UCP rules. Every outbound instruction is subject to automated sanctions screening and name-matching procedures implemented by the instructing bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot transactions for genuine commercial settlement purposes
Plain-vanilla currency forwards under which one leg is EUR
Currency swaps matching the notional, tenor, and interest-payment profile of intercompany debt
FX options (buying or selling) with a documented underlying commercial exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies without active deliverable markets, provided EMIR margin and clearing obligations are observed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Accounts (comptes annuels) with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end (e.g., for 31 December year-end, by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 10,000 (USD 10,800); late filing may trigger court summons and, after repeated default, judicial strike-off or dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Confirmation to the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of the anniversary of the entity's RBE registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 10,000 (USD 10,800) for non-confirmation; intentional omission can lead to criminal fines and imprisonment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax and Net Wealth Tax Declaration (déclaration fiscale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue – Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May following the end of the tax year; extensions may be granted upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of the net tax due plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.5%; failure to file enables ex officio assessment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint an independent auditor (réviseur d'entreprises) if it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total balance sheet EUR 4.4 million, net revenue EUR 8.8 million, and average full-time employees 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP) as codified in the amended Law of 19 December 2002 and the Commercial Code; IFRS is permitted for consolidated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must annually re-confirm all beneficial ownership data with the RBE within one month of the anniversary of its RBE registration. Any shareholding change must be filed within 30 days of the change, and the internal register of beneficial owners must be updated accordingly.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined headline rate in Luxembourg City, comprising 17% corporate income tax on taxable income above EUR 175,000 (15% on the first EUR 175,000), a 7% solidarity surcharge on the corporate income tax, and a 6.75% municipal business tax; the full combined rate fluctuates marginally by commune.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. Effective reliefs: 50% exemption for income from qualifying patent rights (IP regime) subject to nexus ratio and substance requirements; full participation exemption (Soparfi) on qualifying dividends and capital gains where a 10% holding or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost and a 12-month holding requirement are met; notional interest deduction on new equity capital; super-deduction for a first EUR 150,000 of certified digitalisation and carbon-neutral investment expenses for SMEs under the 2024/2025 digital transition measures; group loss relief available for resident group members under the integrated taxation regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 706 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), filed jointly with Form 707 (municipal business tax declaration) and Form 710 (net wealth tax declaration); mandatory electronic filing through the MyGuichet.lu professional e-filing portal (e-Déclarations module), with authentication via Luxembourg LuxTrust certificate or EU eIDAS-compatible credential.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing is due within three months of the end of the financial year; a calendar-year SARL must file by 31 March of the following year. Extension requests are routinely granted, commonly to 31 December of the year following the accounting year, only where the tax return and audited financial statements are prepared by a registered tax professional; corporate income tax prepayments remain due quarterly on 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identity: full corporate name, RCS Luxembourg registration number, and registered office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL with a Luxembourg permanent establishment must enter 'PE' prefix before the name, state the foreign head-office legal form, and provide the foreign commercial register number; a local tax representative may be required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period: opening and closing dates of the financial year covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact PE accounting period; deviations from the head-office accounting year require the ACD's prior written approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit before tax adjustments (résultat comptable avant correction fiscale), reconciled to the Luxembourg GAAP financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE profit attributable under the OECD authorised approach and the applicable double tax treaty (DTA), attaching a branch accounts reconciliation and capital allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses to be added back: fines, excessive directors' fees, 50% of non-deductible entertainment costs, hidden profit distributions, excessive interest, and transfer pricing adjustments (Article 56 LIR).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include any TP adjustments raised in the head office or intra-group benchmark documentation; cross-border hidden distribution adjustments must be supported by the transfer pricing file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carry-forward offset actually applied in the current year, subject to the EUR 1,000,000 annual set-off cap plus 75% of the taxable base exceeding that cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE losses carried under the DTA may only offset Luxembourg-source PE profits; confirm no double-counting of losses in the residence state.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base (bénéfice imposable) after loss offset, from which the 15%/17% corporate income tax brackets and solidarity surcharge are computed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities with a Luxembourg PE must complete the treaty income allocation schedule and declare the full Luxembourg-source taxable base; no aggregation with foreign PE income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax calculation: application of the 15% reduced rate up to EUR 175,000 and 17% on the excess, followed by the 7% solidarity surcharge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The reduced rate applies to a non-resident PE only if the combined worldwide taxable base does not exceed the EUR 175,000 threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax computation (Form 707 reference): taxable value and applicable communal rate of the PE's situs commune.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The municipal business tax is computed on the PE's allocable trade income; non-resident interest and royalty recipients with no Luxembourg PE are not subject to Form 707 unless an exposure exists.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a penal tax (taxe d'attente) from EUR 25 to EUR 25,000, a 10% increase of the assessed tax for negligent or intentional non-disclosure, and statutory default interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid amounts; persistent non-filing permits the ACD to issue an ex officio assessment and, for wilful evasion, criminal fines of EUR 25,000 to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years, with discretionary judgment publication.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax; full exemption applies where the beneficial owner is (i) a Luxembourg resident full-tax company holding directly at least 10% of the share capital for an uninterrupted 12-month period, (ii) an EU/EEA parent company satisfying the same 10%/12-month conditions under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, or (iii) a qualifying non-resident company protected by a bilateral DTA whose reduced rate is 0%, 5%, 10% or 15% depending on the treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate or the parent-subsidiary exemption at source, the Luxembourg paying SARL must obtain, before payment, a valid Luxembourg tax residence certificate (TRC) and the beneficial owner's certificate of residence from the treaty state, together with a written declaration of beneficial ownership and proof of the 10% holding and 12-month holding period; the payer applies the DTA rate on account and the ACD may audit the file. Where withholding was applied at the statutory 15% rate, the non-resident recipient claims a refund via Form 270 before the LAC (Service des Remboursements) of the ACD within the general five-year statute of limitations; the ACD is not bound by a time limit to issue the refund but typically processes within 6 to 12 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes 0% withholding tax on interest and royalties paid to non-residents, including software licence royalties for ERP/CRM cloud subscriptions, subject to the anti-abuse rules (Article 168ter LIR, GAAR, and the Interest and Royalties Directive 2003/49/EC for EU qualifying related companies). Under treaties, source-state taxing rights are generally eliminated at 0% for both interest and royalties, with limited treaties preserving a 5% or 10% residual rate on royalties; no statutory WHT registration obligation exists for the paying entity, but the payer must demonstrate beneficial ownership and economic substance where the recipient is a tax-haven resident.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Master File and Local File under Article 56bis LIR apply to a Luxembourg SARL that is part of an MNE group whose consolidated group revenue equals or exceeds EUR 50 million and whose related-party transactions in the year equal or exceed EUR 1 million; CbC reporting applies at the consolidated group revenue threshold of EUR 750 million and is filed by the ultimate parent or a designated surrogate in Luxembourg.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply the Gulf Cooperation Council style Economic Substance Regulations; substance requirements are embedded in the ACD's beneficial ownership test, the Arsenal Diana and abuse-of-law doctrines, the Soparfi administrative practice, and the OECD BEPS. A vertical ERP/CRM cloud SARL must demonstrate genuine economic substance locally: physical premises in Luxembourg, at least one locally resident director with independent powers, employees performing core operational functions, board minutes taken in Luxembourg, local bank account, and real decision-making; absence of these elements will invalidate tax residence, treaty benefits, the participation exemption, and the IP regime.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully omitting or understating Luxembourg-source subscription and licence revenue, inflating deductible related-party fees, or maintaining two sets of accounting records for the ERP/CRM cloud business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud under Article 214 LIR: fine of EUR 25,000 to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years; mandatory publication of the judgment; 10% administrative increase of the evaded tax; default interest of 0.6% per month; exclusion from public procurement and from holding a professional banking/technology licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause a false return are personally liable for civil restitution of the evaded tax and may be subject to a travel ban (interdiction de quitter le territoire) imposed by the criminal court, asset seizure orders, and imprisonment up to 5 years; the corporate veil is pierced where the SARL is used as a mere façade.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Luxembourg SARL lacking premises, staff, or real management, routing cloud licence fees through a zero-tax jurisdiction with no operational nexus to claim treaty benefits or the participation exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD applies the general anti-abuse rule and the beneficial ownership doctrine to recharacterise the arrangement, deny DTA relief and the parent-subsidiary exemption, and reassess the full corporate income tax, municipal business tax and 15% dividend withholding tax, plus 10% penalty and 0.6% monthly interest; in cases of sham incorporation, the commercial register may order judicial liquidation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors face joint and several civil liability for the company's unpaid taxes where the entity is held to be fictitious; criminal prosecution may attach under the fraud provisions, with travel bans and imprisonment up to 5 years; courts may disallow the limited liability shield of the SARL.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare, update, or submit the TP Master File and Local File, concluding SaaS intercompany licensing agreements without an arm's length benchmark, or shifting profits from the Luxembourg cloud development entity to a related distributor without functional and risk analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD may reconstruct the pricing under the arm's length principle, imposing a primary adjustment plus a secondary adjustment on hidden dividends; penalties for missing documentation include a taxe d'attente up to EUR 25,000 and a 10% increase of the reassessed tax, with monthly default interest; cross-border unilateral adjustments may trigger mutual agreement procedure and potential 25% penalties for gross valuation misstatement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve false TP documentation are personally exposed to criminal fines and imprisonment for tax evasion; in administrative liability actions, managing directors who fail to maintain the mandated documentation may be held personally liable for the resulting tax deficiency and the Luxembourg tax authority may seek enforcement against the directors' personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Beneficial Ownership Filing Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify and file the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) of the SARL in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), or failing to implement AML/KYC procedures on cloud subscription payment flows, including Stripe Billing and Direct Debit rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RBE violations carry criminal fines of EUR 500 to EUR 25,000 for legal persons and EUR 500 to EUR 1,250 for natural persons per default, with repeated offences publishing the sanction and potentially doubling; AML compliance failures under the Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004 attract administrative fines up to EUR 250,000 or 10% of annual turnover for the SARL, and revocation of the electronic payment institution authorisation where applicable; professional certificate holders face suspension.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the designated responsible person for AML are personally liable for failures to implement UBO and KYC procedures; they may receive criminal fines and, in serious or repeated cases, imprisonment from 3 months to 5 years; the CSSF may impose individual fines on directors, and the commercial court may order travel bans pending investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Dividend Withholding and Revenue Repatriation Mismatch
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or interest to a foreign parent or related party without the required statutory or treaty proof, applying a 0% rate without a valid TRC, or routing distributions through a conduit lacking substance to exploit the parent-subsidiary exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer SARL is held liable for the unwithheld 15% dividend withholding tax plus 50% penalty for failure to withhold where the ACD discovers the misuse; a late withholding is compounded by monthly default interest and can be transformed into a criminal charge of misappropriation where funds were distributed knowing the withholding obligation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors who authorised the distribution without ensuring compliance are personally liable for the withheld tax under Luxembourg company law, and the tax authority can pierce the corporate veil to recover the deficiency, impose a travel ban where flight risk is shown, and pursue criminal liability for directors who knowingly circumvented the obligation.
